ashley: Heads up — found partner webhook payload in our ingestion logs that contains a KMS-wrapped blob referencing `projects/partner-prod/locations/global/keyRings/wrk/cryptoKeys/wrap-key`. Thought it was a normal webhook but the body includes `wrapped_credential: <base64>` so likely a wrapped service account key. cc @maria

maria: Ugh. Can you paste the log snippet (redacted) and which cluster/ingest path?

ashley: pasted snippet:
```
{"time":"2026-02-12T14:02:10Z","service":"ingest-proxy","path":"/v1/events/partner-hook","msg":"received payload","payload":{"id":"evt_1234","wrapped_credential":"ZmFrZV9iYXNlNjRf..."}}
```
We see it hitting `ingest-prod-eu` cluster. No errors.

sec-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0422 (severity: medium) — auto-tagged kv:secrets, kms:wrap

jon: Quick triage q's: 1) Is the blob a Vault-wrapped ciphertext or direct Cloud KMS ciphertext? 2) Do we know the partner's entitlement (did they ask us to store wrapped creds)?

ashley: Looks like Cloud KMS ciphertext format — the blob decodes and the proto header hints `projects/partner-prod/.../cryptoKeys/wrap-key`. Partner said they rotate keys but didn't notify us. They likely POSTing wrapped SA JSON for us to decrypt then store in our Vault.

leo: If it's partner-owned KMS key, rotating our Vault transit key won't invalidate their ciphertext. We need to prevent us from accepting it and *also* rotate any stored wrapped creds. Steps: block ingestion path, list accepted_ciphers in Vault, check `secret/partners/*` paths.

sam: I'll run an audit logs query. Command I'm about to run:
```
gcloud logging read 'resource.labels.cluster_name="ingest-prod-eu" AND textPayload:"partner-hook"' --freshness=7d --limit=100
```
I'll paste results in #eng-security-ops when done.

maria: High-level plan: (1) Quarantine the webhook (block writes, leave reads), (2) Discover any stored wrapped blobs in Vault/GCS, (3) Revoke partner SA or ask partner to stop sending, (4) Rotate our Vault transit keys for any secrets we rewrap, (5) Tighten RBAC on the KMS key usage and our Vault access, (6) Postmortem and audit log capture.

ashley: For discovery I grep'd our Vault exports and found 6 entries in `secret/data/partners/partner-a/*` with `wrapped_credential` fields. I exported paths to a snapshot `s3://sec-snapshots/inc-2026-0422/partners-list.txt`

jon: Who will handle revocation with the partner? I can take partner comms. We need them to rotate the KMS key and provide new wrapped blobs (if we still need them) or transition to signed JWTs.

maria: Assignments:
- sam: run full audit query + attach results to INC ticket (ETA 1h)
- ashley: isolate ingestion route (block POSTs) + snapshot listed secrets (ETA 30m)
- jon: contact partner, request KMS key rotation + confirm they stop sending wrapped SA (ETA 2h)
- leo: prepare vault rewrap plan and RBAC delta (ETA 3h)

leo: Vault rewrap plan (draft):
1) For each path in partners-list.txt, pull ciphertext: `vault kv get -format=json secret/data/partners/partner-a/creds`
2) Create a local secure workspace, do not write plaintext to logs
3) Rotate transit key version: `vault write -f transit/keys/partners-rotational/rotate`
4) Rewrap ciphertext to new key version: `vault write transit/rewrap ciphertext=<old_ct> key=partners-rotational`
5) Replace secret with new ciphertext and mark rotated metadata `rotated_by=leo`
6) Run automated test harness for the service that consumes creds

jon: RBAC changes we need on Cloud KMS side: remove broad project-level roles and give only `roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter` scoped to our service accounts + add `condition` to prevent external principals from using the key. I'll draft a least-priv policy.

sam: Audit results: found 12 distinct POSTs from partner IPs in last 48h, 6 unique wrapped blobs stored in Vault, 0 decrypt attempts from our side (no downstream decrypt logged). Uploading logs now.

ashley: Blocked POSTs and added temporary rule to drop any payload containing `wrapped_credential`. Ingest still readable for debugging.

maria: Good. Jon, if partner rotates key, confirm they provide the new public key or rewrapped blob. Until then we should assume those blobs are stale and rotate any secrets we control.

jon: On comms: emailed partner security (sec@partner.com) asking for key rotation & audit trail. Also requested contact for scheduled rotation window.

leo: One more RBAC item: audit logging — ensure Cloud KMS admin & cryptokey accesses are forwarded to our SIEM. GCP audit filter: `protoPayload.serviceName="cloudkms.googleapis.com" AND protoPayload.methodName: "Encrypt" OR "Decrypt"`

maria: Postmortem checklist to capture in INC ticket: root cause, ingestion validation gap, partner onboarding checklist missing, RBAC delta, why we didn't detect KMS key mismatch earlier, timeline, and remediation steps.

sec-bot: Updating incident INC-2026-0422: severity remains medium, status: investigating.

ashley: Quick Q: Should we rotate our own Vault transit key now or wait until partner confirms rotation? My vote: rotate our keys for any secrets we control right away (min blast radius).

maria: Agree. Proceed with internal rotations ASAP for our stored blobs. For partner-owned KMS ciphertext, we'll request rewrapped artifacts or agree to ditch them.

jon: I'll keep partner comms open. If they don't cooperate in 4 hours escalate to account team and legal.

sam: Logs uploaded to the ticket and linked in #eng-security-ops. ETA for full audit export is 2.5h (large window).

leo: I'll stage a maintenance window for rewraps at 2200 UTC — will post exact commands and dry-run in #eng-security before executing.

ashley: Thanks team. Small doc snippet for future onboarding: require explicit key rotation cadence and KMS key principal whitelist + validate ciphertext origin header before accept.

maria: Nice. We'll treat this as a learning item for the partner onboarding checklist. Closing loop: I'll create a follow-up PR with RBAC changes and the audit-forwarder tweak after we confirm rotated secrets.

jon: noted. :thumbsup:

leo: will update the incident ticket with rewrap runbook and dry-run results after 2200 UTC.

sec-bot: Incident INC-2026-0422 updated by maria — added `postmortem:required` tag.
